title: Fields and constructors
summary: What each account remembers, and starting it in a valid state.

say.never: **Fields** are the variables that belong to an object, the facts it remembers, like an account's owner and balance. Each object gets its own copy. On our team, field names end with an underscore `_` so you can tell them from ordinary variables.
say.bit: Fields are an object's own variables. Team standard: field names end in `_`.

marks.label: subclasses can reach it; outside code can't

say.never: The **constructor** is a special method that runs when you write `new`. It has the same name as the class and no return type. Its job is to give every field a starting value. Here, a negative starting balance is replaced by 0, so an account can never begin broken.
say.bit: The constructor runs on `new`. It has the class's name and no return type, and it sets every field.

marks.label: same name as the class, no return type

say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `BankAccount` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.
